previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of Addison’s disease, hypothyroidism, and hypertension, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and fatigue over three days, consistent with an adrenal crisis. She had typical symptoms including salt cravings and headache, and labs showed hyponatremia and hyperkalemia. She received IV hydrocortisone and fluids in the emergency department and was admitted for monitoring. Her condition improved rapidly, with normalization of electrolytes and kidney function. She also experienced benign paroxysmal positional vertigo on admission, which resolved with Epley maneuvers. She was discharged on a rapid hydrocortisone taper, with instructions to resume her baseline prednisone and Florinef, hold metoprolol pending follow-up, and increase Celexa to 20mg daily. She was advised to follow up with her primary care provider for labs and with her endocrinologist, and to seek care if symptoms recurred.

Brief Hospital Course:
In summary, Mrs. ___ is a ___ female with history of 
Addison's disease, hypothyroidism, and HTN who presented with 
abdominal discomfort, nausea and vomiting similar to her 
previous Addisonian crises.
.
# Abdominal discomfort/Nausea/Vomiting: History is consistent 
with her previous Addisonian crises. Hyponatremia and 
hyperkalemia present to corroborate this as well. Unclear 
precipitant; no signs of symptoms of infection. Daughter had PNA 
and URI recently so perhaps she was fighting off a looming 
infection. She also complained of some musculoskeletal pain in 
her RLE (calf area/shin) which she believed she may have ""pulled 
while gardening"". She also has a small bruise over RLE but this 
mild mechanical insult unlikely to provoke an Addisonian flare. 
She denied dysuria, sore throat, headaches, fevers, chills. She 
was continued on IV hydrocortisone and given IVFs for 
resuscitation. Potassium improved from initial 5.6 to 4.8 range 
and her Na of 131 improved to 135 in less than a day. 
Clinically, she stated she felt much better and her nausea, 
emesis and epigastric discomfort had all abated soon after 
admission. She was monitored overnight and she was placed on a 
regular diet which she tolerated very well with a hearty 
appetite. PCP ___ was set up for 4 weeks but patient was 
asked to try to call her PCP for ___ sooner appointment if 
possible.  
.
At time of discharge she was placed on a 2-day taper with PO 
hydrocortisone and instructed to take 25mg every 8 hours on day 
of discharge. The next day she was instructed to then take 25mg 
every 12 hours, then she was told to resume her usual 
5mg PO prednisone and 0.1mg daily Florinef once she had tapered 
for 2 days on hydrocortisone.  
.
# Acute Renal Failure: On admission she had elevated BUN/Cr to 
___ respectively. Creatinine returned to baseline of 1.0 
range by time of discharge. Team felt that her renal decline 
could be attributed to her decreased oral intake in the last two 
days with a predominantly prerenal etiology. As above she was 
placed on continuous  IV hydration and labs were trended 
closely. 
.
# Hyperkalemia: Etiology is secondary to her chronic adrenal 
insufficiency with Addiosonian flare-ups. Potassium level in ED 
was 5.6. Potassium improved to 4.8 to low 5 range after IV 
hydration and IV hydrocortisone therapy. Repeat EKGs were 
largely unchanged from priors and there no new acute concerning 
findings. No acute new peaked T-waves or ST 
depressions/elevations.  
.
#Hypertension: Mrs. ___ was largely normotensive during her 
hospital course. BP was 137/70s in ED and predominantly in the 
110-130s systolic range on the medical floor. She was monitored 
closely and team held metoprolol initially but felt she was 
hemodynamically stable at admission with blood pressures on the 
rise so she was told she could restart her usual home dose and 
as aforementioned she was asked to make a ___ with her PCP 
in the coming weeks.  
.
# Hypothyroidism: She was continued on her usual home dose of 
88mcg Levothyroxine.  
.
#Right lower extremity pain: She complained of pain in her 
achilles tendon area. On additional history she endorsed a 
having prior injuries at her right achilles tendon with 
intermittent pains at baseline. She had been kneeling and 
squatting in her back yard over a 2 day period doing various 
yard work and gardening and expressed that her pain may have 
been related ""overstretching"" her achilles. She also had a small 
bruise over her right tibia which she thinks was from her 
grandson accidentally driving a toy jeep into her leg. Due to 
this persistent complaint of calf pain and some questionable 
edema the team ordered a right lower extremity doppler to ensure 
there were no DVTs, and it was negative. She was given PRN 
Tylenol and Percocet for pain relief and by time of discharge 
her pain was markedly improved, no difficulty with ambulation. 
.
# Depression: She has a longstanding history of depression with 
some additional anxiety as well. She was continued on her usual 
home dose of Celexa daily. Mood and affect were stable and 
appropriate for the entirety of her hospital course. 
.
# Anemia: Normal folate and B12 in the past and her iron panel 
is consistent with anemia of chronic disease. Hematocrit was 
near baseline initially in the 35 range. She was given several 
liters of IVFs and her slight decrease on repeat labs were 
attributed to dilutional effects as she had nonbloody bowel 
movments and no signs of any active bleeding. 

# Fluids, Electrolytes and Nutrition: She was given a regular 
diet, electrolytes were monitored closely as above and she was 
given generous IVFs for rehydration.  
.
# Prophylaxis: She was given SC Heparin TID for DVT prevention 
measures and she was continued on a daily PPI for GI protection. 

.
# Code: She was maintained as a full code status, this was 
confirmed with the patient directly at time of admission.  
.

Discharge Instructions:
It was a pleasure taking care of you here at ___ 
___. 
.
You were admitted with weakness, nausea, vomiting, low sodium 
and high potassium levels. All of these issues were due to a 
flare up of your known Addison's Disease. Additional lab studies 
and a chest x-ray did not reveal any infections. You were given 
IV steroids and IV fluids to help hydrate you. Your sodium and 
postassium abnormalities corrected and by the day of discharge 
your nausea, emesis and generalized fatigue had gone away.  
Although we did not find a definite trigger for your Addison's 
flare up it is quite possible that you may have been on the 
verge of getting a sickness and your body (immune system) was 
able to fight it off.  
.
Because of your right lower leg pain you had a lower extremity 
ultrasound imaging study which showed no evidence of any blood 
clots in your leg. The pain was felt to be secondary to some 
residual achilles tendon pain after recent strenuous activity 
with gardening and yard work. 
.
If you have any fevers, chills, dizziness, lightheadedness, 
additional vomiting, excessive diarrhea, abdominal pain/cramps, 
headaches, confusion, heart palpitations, worsening lower 
extremity pain or any additional health concerns please contact 
your primary care M.D. or return to the emergency room. 
.
MEDICATION INSTRUCTIONS/CHANGES:
* You have been placed back on your usual home metoprolol 
medication as your blood pressures have been increasing and are 
in a safe range for you to restart this medication. Please 
discuss this medication with your PCP at ___ as well. 
.
*You have been placed on a slow taper of Hydrocortisone. Please 
take as instructed and when the taper is complete in 2 days time 
you can return to your usual daily Prednisone and Florinef 
regimen
.
*Otherwise, please continue to take all of your other home 
medications as previously prescribed. 
.
